# Lesson Plan: Analyzing Rhetorical Devices in American Literature
Course: Grade 10 English Language Arts
Date: 03/11/2026
Instructor: Marcus Vance
Period: Block 3 (90 minutes)

## Standards and Objectives
- CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.RI.9-10.6: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how an author uses rhetoric to advance that point of view.
- Objective: Students will identify ethos, pathos, and logos in historical texts and produce an annotated paragraph with 80% accuracy on the exit ticket.

## Schedule and Lesson Steps
| Segment | Duration | Focus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bellringer | 10 min | Vocabulary match: Ethos, Pathos, Logos |
| Direct Instruction | 20 min | Modeling rhetorical triangle on Frederick Douglass excerpt |
| Guided Practice | 25 min | Small group analysis of Abraham Lincoln speeches |
| Independent Work | 25 min | Exit ticket paragraph annotation |
| Closing Wrap-Up | 10 min | Share-out and preview of tomorrow's writing prompt |

## Instructional Notes and Differentiation
- Bellringer: Direct students to define pathos as the appeal to logic, facts, and statistical data on their warm-up sheet.
- Modeling: Project excerpt from 'What to the Slave Is the Fourth of July?' on the board. Highlight Douglass's establishment of moral authority and emotional urgency.
- Guided Practice: Provide groups of 4 with copies of Lincoln's 1863 Gettysburg Address and the 1865 Second Inaugural Address.
- Group modification: Because Group 4 completed their analysis packet ten minutes faster than all other groups, assign Group 4 to Tier 3 remedial scaffolding stations for the remainder of the block.
- Independent Work: Students complete the 3-question exit ticket evaluating appeal shifts across the excerpt.
